router_distinctions:
Select the tier whose capabilities best fit the task. Under-escalating is just as costly as over-escalating.

CRITICAL: The 'agent' tier spawns multiple AI agents in parallel — it is ONLY for tasks that need parallel independent work. A task being 'complex' or 'multi-step' does NOT mean it needs agents. Most tasks, even complex ones, should go to sonnet or opus.

When in doubt between sonnet/opus/agent: if one model can handle it step-by-step, use sonnet or opus. Only use agent when the task has independent workstreams that benefit from parallelism.

tiers.name: haiku
tiers.router_label: Casual conversation, simple factual questions, short summaries, translations, web searches, running scheduled jobs, invoking tools, simple file creation, quick edits, toggling settings

tiers.name: sonnet
tiers.router_label: Code review, debugging, explaining complex concepts, research synthesis, editing code files, implementing features, fixing bugs, creating scripts, writing tests, multi-file changes, create scheduled jobs, create reminders, multi-step tasks that a single developer can handle sequentially

tiers.name: opus
tiers.router_label: Architecture design, system-level reasoning, complex trade-off analysis, large-scale refactoring, implementing complex features, redesigning system architecture, building new modules from scratch, complex multi-step tasks requiring deep thinking

tiers.name: agent
tiers.router_label: ONLY for tasks explicitly requesting a team of agents, or requiring parallel independent workstreams that CANNOT be done sequentially by one model (e.g. 'build a full app with frontend + backend + tests simultaneously', 'write 5 articles at once', 'research 3 topics in parallel'). If one model can handle it step-by-step, use sonnet or opus instead.
